{
  "verdict": "fix",
  "issues": [
    "The error format is only an example body; there is no schema or enumeration of error codes, so the uniform error contract is underspecified and clients cannot rely on stable structure beyond the example.",
    "The request bodies for POST and PATCH are only examples; no request schema is defined, leaving required vs optional fields, allowed updatable fields, and validation rules undocumented for consumers.",
    "GET /tasks returns a bare array, which is acknowledged as making pagination a breaking change; for a collection API this is a real evolution risk.",
    "No server-error handling or 500 status is specified, so the behavior for internal failures is undefined, even though the proposal claims a status code mapping.",
    "PATCH updates can silently overwrite concurrent modifications; there is no ETag/If-Match or other concurrency control, which is a risk for a CRUD API where multiple clients may update the same resource.",
    "The spec is a custom JSON structure rather than a standard like OpenAPI, so the claim of a machine-readable contract is weak: standard tooling, validators, and code generators cannot consume it."
  ],
  "suggestions": [
    "Define a formal error schema (e.g., code, message, details) and enumerate all possible error codes with their meanings; include an example per endpoint.",
    "Add explicit request body schemas for POST and PATCH, distinguishing required fields for creation and allowed updatable fields (e.g., title, description, completed, not id/createdAt/updatedAt).",
    "Change GET /tasks to return an object with an items array (and optionally total) from the start, or document a versioned breaking-change policy for adding pagination later.",
    "Add a 500 status code and a generic internal error format, or explicitly state that server errors are out of scope.",
    "Support ETags and If-Match on PATCH, or document a concurrency strategy (e.g., last-write-wins) to avoid silent data loss.",
    "Express the spec in OpenAPI 3.x (or at least as a proper JSON Schema) so it can be used with standard API tooling and validators."
  ]
}
